title: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
name: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
description: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct is an instruction-tuned 8B-parameter member of the Llama 3 family designed for production single-GPU deployments, multilingual chat, RAG, and agent workloads where a balance of quality and cost is required.

downloads.notes: Official model card and access point for weights and tokenizer; authoritative source for checkpoints and license.

runtime_compatibility.notes: Loading and fine-tuning supported; heavy for large context without optimized kernels. Official model card points to integration examples.
Recommended for high-throughput single-GPU/cluster inference and long-context workloads; community docs include Llama 3 guidance.
Community GGUF builds enable CPU/edge inference for 8B with quantization (AWQ/GGUF); use quantized artifacts for performance.
Vendor conversion required for GPU-optimized inference; recommended for high-throughput production GPU deployments.
Developer runtimes with community support; suitable for local testing and packaging.

deployment.recommended_quantization: AWQ or GPTQ (8-bit or 4-bit variants) validated on held-out tasks to balance memory reduction and instruction-following fidelity; prefer AWQ/GPTQ community pipelines with evaluation against development tasks before production rollout.

license_info.name: Llama 3.1 Community License
license_info.notes: Licensing and permitted uses are authoritative on the official model card; do not deploy for uses outside allowed license terms.

best_for: Instruction-following chat and agent backends for mid-scale production (single-GPU) with moderate throughput requirements.
RAG systems where a moderately-sized dense model is preferable for cost-quality trade-offs.
On-premise self-hosting where data control and fine-tuning matter and 8B footprint fits infra constraints.
avoid_for: Highest-quality multi-turn reasoning where 70B+ variants demonstrably outperform on edge-case reasoning tasks.
Extremely latency-sensitive microservices with sub-10ms SLOs.
Workloads that mandate vendor-hosted SLA-only models or have incompatible licensing constraints.
engineering_snapshot.recommended_use_case: Cost-conscious production chat/agent deployments requiring instruction-following, multilingual coverage, and ability to run on single high-memory GPU or quantized CPU for edge.
deployment_risks: Quantization-induced silent quality regressions on instruction-following or code generation tasks.
Out-of-memory (OOM) or high latency spikes when running 128K context workloads on resource-constrained GPUs.
failure_modes: Severe quality/latency degradation if context window is not aggressively capped or properly sharded.
Tokenization and encoding issues from using incorrect or non-standard tokenizers.
common_mistakes: Over-relying on community quantized artifacts without systematic task-level validation.
Attempting large-context inference without FlashAttention or vLLM-optimized memory kernels.
operational_notes: GQA reduces inference memory and compute for this family’s 8B variant relative to naive attention implementations — ensure runtime supports or emulates GQA-efficient kernels for best performance.
Quantized GGUF/AWQ/GPTQ builds reduce GPU/CPU memory but require task-specific validation; measure instruction-following fidelity and code generation quality before production rollout.

Single-GPU deployment is realistic with FP16 or INT8/GPTQ quantization on modern consumer/professional GPUs; for high-throughput or long-context (128K) use vLLM with multi-GPU or high-memory GPU instances.

Use vLLM or TensorRT-LLM conversions to leverage FlashAttention/optimized GPU kernels for throughput gains. For CPU/edge, use llama.cpp GGUF quantized artifacts with AWQ/GPTQ. Monitor latency-vs-quality trade-offs after quantization.
Use the official 128K tokenizer artifact from the model card to avoid tokenization mismatch; tokenizer/vocab mismatch causes encoding and downstream fidelity issues.
Prompting format: follow the instruction templates documented in model card discussions to match instruction-tuned behavior.

Variant differentiation (Identity): Parameter count (8B) is the primary differentiator vs. 3.1-70B/405B — this variant targets single-GPU or light multi-GPU serving with lower infra cost while preserving instruction-tuned behavior; many lower-level spec fields are available only in official model card artifacts and should be sourced per-deployment.

Variant differentiation (File Formats): 8B instruct variant has the broadest community availability of quantized/edge formats relative to larger variants; prefer official safetensors for conversion to GGUF/GPTQ/AWQ to preserve fidelity.

Variant differentiation (Hardware Requirements): Compared with 70B/405B, the 8B instruct variant is realistically deployable on a single high-memory GPU with quantization, enabling lower infra complexity and cost for production chat/agent services.

Variant differentiation (Downloads): Use the official Hugging Face model card as the canonical download and metadata source for this variant; community mirrors exist but validate checksums against the official card.

Variant differentiation (Runtime Compatibility): 3.1-8B instruct is supported by the widest set of runtimes with mature community conversion paths; preferred production runtimes are vLLM for server-side throughput and llama.cpp/GGUF for edge/CPU use.

Variant differentiation (Deployment): 8B instruct is the most pragmatic variant for single-GPU production or CPU-deployed quantized instances; choose quantization level based on quality validation and latency targets.
Variant differentiation (License): Always consult the model card before commercial deployment—license terms can differ between base, instruct, and safety variants.
Variant differentiation (Status): production (officially published instruct checkpoint intended for deployment).
